questions.text: In the input “the [MASK] chased the mouse,” which visible words can a standard bidirectional BERT encoder use to predict the masked token?

options.B: Only “chased the mouse” after the mask.
options.C: No visible words; only the mask token itself.
options.D: Visible words both before and after the mask.

questions.explanation: Bidirectional attention allows the masked position to use visible context on both sides.

questions.text: An MLM-selected token is left unchanged under BERT’s 80/10/10 rule. Should its original token ID still be used as a prediction target?

options.A: Yes; selection determines the target even when the input is unchanged.
options.B: No; every unchanged input token must use the ignore-index label.
options.C: No; its label must be replaced with the [MASK] token ID.
options.D: Yes; but only after replacing its input with a random token.

questions.explanation: Selected positions contribute original-token targets regardless of whether they are masked, randomized, or left unchanged.

questions.text:
What are input_ids and labels after this code?

```python
tokens = [5, 8]
input_ids = list(tokens)
labels = [-100] * len(tokens)
i = 1
labels[i] = tokens[i]
r = 0.85
if r < 0.8:
    input_ids[i] = 99
elif r < 0.9:
    input_ids[i] = 3  # supplied random replacement
```
questions.explanation: r=0.85 enters the random-replacement branch, changing input ID8 to3; the target remains the original8 and the unselected position remains ignored.
